neighbours.label: an upbeat evaluative build-up in chatty newsletter/promo prose ('what a ___ start', 'a big year', 'a whole lot more exciting')
fire: Well, what a wonderful start to the term we have had at the school!
The young singer is having a huge year, with two albums and a tour.
Your weekend baking just got a whole lot more exciting with this recipe.
What a brilliant evening it was for everyone who came to the fair!
It has been such an amazing season for our under-twelves team.
Our garden club had a fantastic month, with record crowds at the show.
Wow, what a busy and rewarding week it has been in Year 4!
This summer is shaping up to be a really big one for the local theatre.
quiet: Well, the term started on Monday and classes are now under way at the school.
The young singer released two albums this year and will go on tour.
Your weekend baking needs flour, sugar and three eggs for this recipe.
The evening began at six for everyone who came to the fair.
The season ended in May for our under-twelves team.
Our garden club met four times this month, and the show is in June.
This week Year 4 studied fractions and visited the library.
This summer the local theatre will stage two plays in July.

notes: Card: no single token; peaks on ' a' in 'what a fantastic start', ' year' in 'a big year', ' exciting' in 'a whole lot more exciting', ' century', ' such'. Near misses keep the newsletter style but state the same facts flatly.
